newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia loan curbs may last a few years - Anwar.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia loan curbs may last a few years - Anwar.

text.p: Malaysia's curbs on bank loans for property and stock purchases may be imposed for a few more years, Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Tuesday.

"This pre-emptive measure is taken before the situation gets worse, and we have made projections for 1998 and 2000," the national news agency Bernama quoted him as saying. "Therefore, loans have to be curbed for two, three, even four years."
Bank Negara Malaysia announced on March 28 it was requiring banks and finance companies to trim exposure to the property sector to 20 percent of total outstanding loans from nearly 30 percent now.
New restrictions were also placed on financing stock purchases.
The curbs on property loans were aimed at preventing a speculative bubble within that sector.
